title: Playing with Louis Armstrong's first six-piece band
summary: Dawson recounts Armstrong's start at fish fries, his first band at a hotel with Dawson on bass, and the trombonists he used.

story.theme_name: Working with and around Louis Armstrong
story.community_name: Playing with and around Louis Armstrong

blocks.x: Well, it's like I said, I played, when I was playing, I was, when I played with Rene, that's practically most every, every dance he played for outside, dances he had to advertise. People hire, when they hire a band, they hire for the advertising, too, you see. They give you two dollars extra for that advertising. Did Rene ever buck against Louis Armstrong? Oh, Armstrong, practically yes. Well, Armstrong, he didn't, he didn't, didn't much, he didn't do much advertising. Uh-huh. You know, because when Armstrong came out of Jones' home, he, uh, he, uh, he started at, uh, Joe Segretta. Right up here on Liberty and Pedida. Uh-huh. But he started a little fish fries, he called fish fries, and he was playing a little, uh, say a trio, a piano, trumpet, and drum, clarinet. Uh-huh. And, uh, uh, Joe Segretta was running, running that fish fries at Liberty and Pedida. Well, then he had a little brass trumpet. They say trumpet is a cornet. A little sharp one, you know, what he came out of Jones' home with. And after he started, uh, going by Maurice, uh, got good with Guellarine and got, then got him a real trumpet. And, uh, he, he, first he started a six-piece band. Well, I played with him a good little while, too, you see, with, uh, Louis Armstrong. We played the first job, I know, to play a heavy job, was at the Junk Hotel, when we was wearing uniform, them, you know, like them, uh, uh, regular, uh, heavy coats, you know? Band coats with the high collars. Like the market band. Yeah, like, with caps. Uh-huh. And then heavy coats. Like the Imperial.

Well, uh, they'd have six pieces. We went to the Junk Hotel and played there. Well, he had Son Thomas playing guitar. I was playing bass. He had, uh, Dominic Remy on the trumpet. They had two trumpets. He had T-Boy Remy with him. And he had a fella called Pill on the clarinet. He died. He had a little bow-legged fella called Pill. Well, after that, well, Louis played around spot jobs around different places. And then, that's when he went up the line. Joe Oliver got with Joe Oliver. And him and Joe Oliver formed a band with Chicago. And they worked together with two of them in the same band until they fell out. Then Louis went his way and got his own band. Joe Oliver had his until he died.
And, uh, did he have a trombone down here, Louis? Used the trombone much?

Well, uh, yes. I used to use trombone. He had, uh, uh, let's see. His fellow was supposed to be a good trombone player. Uh, Jack Carey played with him a while on the trombone. He was an old trombone player. And he had, uh, uh, a fella called Benny Raphael. That was a pre-old fella. He was a good trombone player. Benny Raphael. And, uh, that's all I know. Uh-huh. Most of them.
